To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified new genetic variants associated with type 2 diabetes in the Singapore Chinese Health study.

we found that 20 out of 69 known T2D associated index SNPs are significantly associated with T2DM risk and the risk score is significantly associated with TDM risk in the Singapore Chinese Health study population.
we have found that the genetic risk of type 2 diabetes is higher in Singapore Chinese compared to Caucasians, but that the risk is lower compared to the risk in Singapore Malays and Indians.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genetic risk factors in type 1 and type 2 diabetes in Singapore, a multi-ethnic population with a high prevalence of diabetes.
the identification and understanding of the genetic and environmental factors that contribute to T2D in the Singapore Chinese.
identifying the genetic and environmental determinants of T2D in Asian populations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
genetic risk factors in T2D are complex and that environmental factors are likely to be important modifiers of disease susceptibility.
T2D risk in Singapore Chinese is not fully explained by known genetic factors.
the genetic basis of T2D is complex, and is likely to involve both common variants and rare variants, and both genetic and environmental factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
genetic risk is a small part of a complex picture.
while diabetes risk in Singaporean Chinese involves genetic variants that are similar to those found in European populations, most of the disease risk remains unexplainable.
the genetic architecture for type 2 diabetes is complex, with multiple genetic variants of modest effect size contributing to disease risk, and with a strong environmental component.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic architecture of T2D is complex, and the genetic risk of this disease is not fully explained by the known common genetic variants.
the genetics of T2D are complex and involve both common and rare variants.
genetic variants in T2D susceptibility genes have not been able to explain the rapid increase in T2D incidence in Singapore.
